Preliminary patch testing was done with full strength Ethyl Methacrylate and the actual testing used open and semiocclusive patches, with positive and negative controls. No positive reactions occurred from exposure to Ethyl Methacrylate either during the induction or challenge phase of the test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.05-0.5% pentyl salicylate in base cream or 99% ethanol; closed patch with 1 cm² lint and cellophane disc, covered with plaster; 24-48 h occlusion on back, forearm, or inside upper arm; read 30 min after removal; 155 patients (316 tests).
evidence.support_text: Closed patch tests with 0.05-0.5% pentyl salicylate in base cream or 99% ethanol on 155 patients (316 tests) resulted in erythema in 8 cases (Takenaka et al., 1986).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1968; 273 chronic dermatitis patients; Schorr
evidence.support_text: Diagnostic tests for skin sensitization show a reaction rate of 0.7% when tested in 1968 on 273 chronic dermatitis patients by Schorr for parabens.

evidence.experimental_conditions: International Contact Dermatitis Research Group; 4,825 patients (male and female, white); occlusive patch for 48 h; evaluation at 24, 48, 72 h after removal; concentration 2%; vehicle aqueous
evidence.support_text: In a diagnostic patch test study by the International Contact Dermatitis Research Group with 4,825 white patients, formalin (aqueous) at 2% gave 169 positive reactors (3.5%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: North American Contact Dermatitis Group; 1,200 patients (male and female, black and white); occlusive patch for 48 h; evaluation at 24, 48, 72 h after removal; concentration 2%; vehicle aqueous
evidence.support_text: In a diagnostic patch test study by the North American Contact Dermatitis Group with 1,200 patients, formalin (aqueous) at 2% gave 43 positive reactors (4%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% kojic acid in cosmetic product or medicinal cream; applied to human skin
evidence.support_text: Case studies have reported contact dermatitis in patients using cosmetic products or medicinal creams containing 1% kojic acid. In a therapeutic study for melasma, the side effect of 1% kojic acid treatment was contact allergy.
A 43-year-old man (case no.2) with foot dermatitis was patch tested to standard, shoe and textile series and showed positive reactions to mercapto mix.
A 45-year-old non-atopic man with foot dermatitis showed positive patch test reactions to quinoline mix and dyes (Case no. 1).
A 66-year-old woman diagnosed with heparin-induced eosinophilic panniculitis due to enoxaparin injection had a positive patch test to enoxaparin, confirming the diagnosis.
In a group of 16 patients with foot dermatitis patch tested to shoe and textile allergens, 3 showed positive reactions to PTBP-formaldehyde resin.
In a group of 16 patients with foot dermatitis patch tested to shoe and textile allergens, 4 showed positive reactions to mercapto mix.
In a group of 16 patients with foot dermatitis patch tested to shoe and textile allergens, 4 showed positive reactions to para-phenylenediamine.

In a patient with contact dermatitis from triphenyl phosphite (TPP), no reaction was observed when patch tested with triphenyl phosphate, indicating lack of cross-reactivity and a negative skin sensitization outcome for triphenyl phosphate.
In a study of 53 patients patch tested for foot dermatitis over December 1995–December 1997, 3 patients showed a positive reaction to PTBP-formaldehyde resin (Table 1).
In a study of 53 patients patch tested for foot dermatitis over December 1995–December 1997, 4 patients showed a positive reaction to mercapto mix (Table 1).
Patch tests with cotrimoxazole were reported to give positive topical provocations in patients with cotrimoxazole-induced fixed eruptions.

Two test subjects had positive patch test reactions to Lanolin product C and cream C. The test subject with a ++ reaction to cream C had a negative ROAT and also healed fast when applying cream C on SLS induced dermatitis, hence presenting no correlation between patch test and ROAT outcome for cream C.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.010–0.015 ml of Thymol (0.10–0.15 mg); readings up to 96 h
evidence.support_text: A 51-year-old man with acute dermatitis after exposure to wood was patch tested with 0.010–0.015 ml of Thymol and showed no reaction up to 96 h. Ten controls also had no reaction (Bleumink et al. 1973).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.1% petrolatum, Finn Chambers, readings at 2 and 3 days, according to ICDRG guidelines
evidence.support_text: Patch tests performed with the components of Medicated Cream for Hands and Fingers N® cream showed positive to DL-α-tocopheryl nicotinate (DL-α-TN) (0.1% pet.) (+) with readings at 2 and 3 days according to ICDRG guidelines in a 32-year-old woman with a history of contact dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.2% aq., readings on day 3 and day 5
evidence.support_text: The patient was patch tested to the 27 components provided by the moisturizer manufacturer and showed a positive reaction (++) on day 3 and 5 to cystamine bis-lactamide 0.2% aq. This indicates an allergic contact dermatitis from this compound.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.25% aq., patch test reading at D2 and D3
evidence.support_text: The patient, who had atopic dermatitis since age 5, was patch tested with guava tea extract 0.25% aq. and showed positive reactions at D2 and D3. Nine healthy subjects patch tested as controls with 0.25% guava tea extract were negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.25% aqueous solution, reading at D2 and D3
evidence.support_text: A 17-year-old atopic dermatitis patient had positive patch test reactions to guava tea extract 0.25% aq. at D2 and D3; 9 healthy controls tested with the same extract were negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.25% in aqueous solution, readings at day 2 and day 3
evidence.support_text: A 17-year-old atopic dermatitis patient showed positive patch test reactions at D2 and D3 to guava tea extract 0.25% aq. Nine healthy subjects patch tested as controls with the same preparation were negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 763 eczema patients; testing with lim-1-OOH and lim-2-OOH; study from reference [34]
evidence.support_text: A published human patch test study with 763 eczema patients reported that 18 individuals responded to lim-1-OOH and 13 to lim-2-OOH [34]. This prevalence is in accordance with the potency ranking obtained in the current COCAT study.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 8% in petrolatum, eczema patient (alone)
evidence.support_text: A pilot multicenter study gave a reaction in a patient tested alone at 8% methyl heptine carbonate. The table row for reference 42 shows 1 out of 1 patient reacted at 8% in petrolatum, but this concentration was considered irritant.

evidence.experimental_conditions: acetophenone azine 1% in petrolatum, patch test, reading day not specified.
evidence.support_text: A 6-year-old soccer player with acetophenone azine-induced shin pad and sports shoes dermatitis reacted positively to acetophenone azine in petrolatum at 1% on patch testing (Besner Morin et al., as cited).

evidence.experimental_conditions: ACMO 0.5% in petrolatum; patch test reading on standard days (D2/D4); the control group included 25 eczema patients without prior exposure to the suspected glue
evidence.support_text: Twenty-five controls with ACMO 0.5% pet. were performed. Twenty-five consecutive eczema patients attending three contact dermatitis patch test departments to be investigated for unrelated eczema without previous exposure to the suspected glue agreed to act as controls. Twenty-one were negative, three were positive, and one developed a late reaction to it (on D18). The positive controls involved three individuals under investigation for reactions to long-lasting nail polish and other manicure products with acrylates who also had strong concomitant reactions to many acrylates such as HEMA, HPMA, and EGDMA, among others.

evidence.experimental_conditions: BHT 2% in petrolatum, standard patch testing procedure
evidence.support_text: In a Danish study based both on consecutively patch-tested patients at a dermatological clinic and on estimates of exposure derived from a national database on chemical products (FLYVHOLM and MENNÉ, 1990) the sensitizing risk of BHT was evaluated. No positive patch test reaction was found to BHT 2% in petrolatum in 1336 consecutively tested eczema patients.

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentration 1% pet.; reading at D3
evidence.support_text: A 23-month-old child with eczema was patch tested (European standard series, corticosteroids series, rubber series and samples of the diapers) and showed at D3 a + reaction to cyclohexyl thiophthalimide 1% pet. and to the rubber bands of diapers.

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentration not specified
evidence.support_text: Another case study reported hand eczema in a diesel mechanic that was exacerbated with the use of moist toilet paper. The diesel oil and the toilet paper each contained trade name mixtures of MCI/MI biocides. Positive reactions to Methylisothiazolinone were observed with patch testing.

evidence.experimental_conditions: DMAPA at concentrations as low as 0.05% in petrolatum, tested in 12 patients (15 total, 3 not tested)
evidence.support_text: In the study by Pigatto et al, 12 patients with eczema were further tested with DMAPA at concentrations as low as 0.05% in petrolatum. All except 3 patients, who were not tested, had 2+ or 3+ reaction to DMAPA, indicating positive allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: European baseline series, preservatives series, and occupational products; 26-yr-old man
evidence.support_text: A 26-year-old man with eczema after exposure to wall paint and façade renders had ++ and +++ reactions on day2 and day4 to Methylisothiazolinone (2000 ppm aq.) when tested with European baseline series, preservatives series, and occupational products.

evidence.experimental_conditions: European multicenter study (EECDRG), patients with eczema, 1996–2000
evidence.support_text: European multicenter studies found positive reactions to FM in 9.7% (EECDRG, 1996–2000) of patients with eczema.

evidence.experimental_conditions: European multicenter study (ESSCA), patients with eczema, 2002–2003
evidence.support_text: European multicenter studies found positive reactions to FM in 7.1% (ESSCA, 2002–2003) of patients with eczema.

evidence.experimental_conditions: German baseline series; 28-yr-old woman with history of atopic dermatitis
evidence.support_text: A 28-year-old woman with hand eczema had a + reaction to Methylisothiazolinone (0.2% aq.) on day2 and day3 when tested with the German baseline series.

evidence.experimental_conditions: ICDRG standard patch test series; 1% PCMC in petrolatum; reactions scored per ICDRG recommendations; consecutive eczema patients
evidence.support_text: Andersen and Veien (1985) tested 671 consecutive eczema patients with the ICDRG standard series. PCMC, 1% in petrolatum, was tested on 671 patients and no positive reactions were observed. PCMC was withdrawn from the patch test battery after 3 months due to the lack of reactions observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: ICDRG standard patch test series; 2% PCMC in petrolatum; reactions scored per ICDRG recommendations; consecutive eczema patients
evidence.support_text: Andersen and Hamann (1984a) tested 1462 consecutive eczema patients with the ICDRG standard patch test series, which included 2% PCMC in petrolatum. Reactions were scored according to the recommendations of the ICDRG (Wilkinson et al. 1970). Of 1462 patients tested, only 5 had positive patch test results and 6 had irritant reactions; none of the positive results were clinically explainable.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with 'Hamamelis virg. 10% in petrolatum' in 280 consecutive eczema patients.
evidence.support_text: In a series of 280 consecutive eczema patients, no positive patch test reactions to Hamamelis virginiana extract at 10% in petrolatum were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test with European standard series, carba mix 3% in petrolatum (assumed), according to ICDRG guidelines
evidence.support_text: In the total study period (1985-1999), 904 cement workers with a history of eczema were patch tested with the European standard series. Carba mix 3% elicited a positive patch test reaction in 90 patients, representing 13% of the 678 patients who had at least one positive reaction (Table 1 total row; carba mix was not tested after 1992).

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test with European standard series, MBT 2% in petrolatum (assumed), according to ICDRG guidelines
evidence.support_text: In the total study period (1985-1999), 904 cement workers with a history of eczema were patch tested with the European standard series. MBT (mercaptobenzothiazole) 2% elicited a positive patch test reaction in 27 patients, representing 4% of the 678 patients who had at least one positive reaction (Table 1 total row).

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test with European standard series, mercapto mix 2% in petrolatum (assumed), according to ICDRG guidelines
evidence.support_text: In the total study period (1985-1999), 904 cement workers with a history of eczema were patch tested with the European standard series. Mercapto mix 2% elicited a positive patch test reaction in 32 patients, representing 5% of the 678 patients who had at least one positive reaction (Table 1 total row).

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test with European standard series, thiuram mix 1% in petrolatum (assumed), according to ICDRG guidelines
evidence.support_text: In the total study period (1985-1999), 904 cement workers with a history of eczema were patch tested with the European standard series. Thiuram mix 1% elicited a positive patch test reaction in 251 patients, representing 37% of the 678 patients who had at least one positive reaction (Table 1 total row).

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test with henna (plant material); patient with palpebral eczema
evidence.support_text: Perez and coworkers [60] reported a patient with palpebral eczema and a strong positive patch test reaction to henna, which was used to dye her hair.

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test, ICDRG standard series, dose not reported, vehicle not reported, reading at 48 and 96 h, eczema quiescent
evidence.support_text: In a study of Nottinghamshire coal miners with eczematous skin problems, 35 miners were patch tested with the ICDRG standard series including fragrance mix and its components. Reactions to cinnamaldehyde (dose and vehicle not reported) were seen in 14% of the miners at 48 and 96 h.

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test, ICDRG standard series, dose not reported, vehicle not reported, reading at 48 and 96 h, eczema quiescent
evidence.support_text: In the same study, 55 male non-miners were patch tested. Reactions to cinnamaldehyde were seen in 7% of them.

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test, ICDRG standard series, dose not reported, vehicle not reported, reading at 48 and 96 h, eczema quiescent
evidence.support_text: Thirty female non-miners were also patch tested; no effects in the women were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test, London hairdressers with eczema, 1%-2.5% concentration
evidence.support_text: London hairdressers (n = 143) were patch tested with eczema. Ammonium Thioglycolate (1%-2.5% concentrations) showed positive results displayed as eczematous atopic (4 of 45, 9%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch tests; 228 eczema patients
evidence.support_text: Mitchell et al. (1982) reported that patch tests conducted on 228 eczema patients resulted in 1% positive reactions to citral.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Tested 1% pet., consecutive eczema patients, July 1981 to June 1982, using Finn Chambers on Scanpor.
evidence.support_text: From July 1981 to June 1982, 476 consecutive eczema patients were patch tested with Cytox® 3522 (1% pet.) without any positive reactions being elicited.

evidence.experimental_conditions: tested at 10%; 590 eczema patients
evidence.support_text: Expressed bergamot oil caused reactions in 0.5% of 590 eczema patients when tested at 10% in a human patch test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: TRUE Test, additional allergen series, and personal products; 48-yr-old man
evidence.support_text: A 48-year-old man with eczema had ++ and ++ reactions to Methylisothiazolinone on day3 and day7 following testing with TRUE Test, additional allergen series, and personal products.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5% methyl dihydrojasmonate in petrolatum applied to the backs of 318 eczema patients for 2 days, scored on days 3, 4, and 5–7 after patch removal.
evidence.support_text: Patch tests were conducted with 5% methyl dihydrojasmonate in petrolatum on 318 eczema patients. The test material was applied to the backs of subjects for 2 days. The sites were scored on days 3 and 4 and 5–7 days after patch removal. No reactions were observed (Paulsen and Andersen, 2005).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 22 eczema patients with prior patch test reaction to cinnamaldehyde; 0.02% cinnamaldehyde in ethanol applied twice daily for 2 weeks
evidence.support_text: In a ROAT, 22 eczema patients who had previously reacted to cinnamaldehyde in a patch test were exposed to 0.02% cinnamaldehyde in ethanol twice daily for two weeks; no reactions were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 22 eczema patients with prior patch test reaction to cinnamaldehyde; 0.1% cinnamaldehyde in ethanol applied twice daily for 2 weeks (weeks 3-4)
evidence.support_text: In a ROAT, 22 eczema patients who had previously reacted to cinnamaldehyde in a patch test were exposed to 0.1% cinnamaldehyde in ethanol twice daily for two weeks; 8 patients reacted.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 22 eczema patients with prior patch test reaction to cinnamaldehyde; 0.8% cinnamaldehyde in ethanol applied twice daily for 2 weeks (weeks 5-6)
evidence.support_text: In a ROAT, 22 eczema patients who had previously reacted to cinnamaldehyde in a patch test were exposed to 0.8% cinnamaldehyde in ethanol twice daily for two weeks; 5 patients reacted.

evidence.assay_type: covalent binding assay with bovine serum albumin
evidence.experimental_conditions: bovine serum albumin; presence of thiol, amine, alcohol nucleophiles
evidence.support_text: Thiol nucleophiles decreased the extent of covalent binding to the model protein bovine serum albumin, while amine and alcohol nucleophiles had no effect, suggesting reactivity with cysteine of proteins. This implies apalutamide covalently binds to BSA.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Incubated with human plasma; [³H]Analogue 1
evidence.support_text: Analogue 1, which possesses the spirocyclobutane, as apalutamide does, but has a cyanophenyl in place of the cyanopyridine, was also tested in human plasma for comparison. It demonstrated substantially lower binding than apalutamide.

evidence.assay_type: Covalent binding by radiolabeled compound to model protein
evidence.experimental_conditions: Incubated with bovine serum albumin; [³H]apalutamide; presence/absence of nucleophiles tested
evidence.support_text: As with plasma, apalutamide bound to BSA to a greater degree than enzalutamide (approximately six-fold). Thiol nucleophiles GSH and N-acetylcysteine caused a decrease, but not abolition, of apalutamide covalent binding, while amine (N-acetyllysine) and alcohol (N-acetylserine) had no impact.

evidence.assay_type: Covalent binding by radiolabeled compound to model protein
evidence.experimental_conditions: Incubated with bovine serum albumin; [³H]enzalutamide
evidence.support_text: As with plasma, apalutamide bound to BSA to a greater degree than enzalutamide (approximately six-fold). The nucleophiles had no effect on the low enzalutamide binding, except for the small effect of N-acetylcysteine.

evidence.assay_type: covalent binding to bovine serum albumin
evidence.experimental_conditions: Binding to bovine serum albumin through cysteine residue
evidence.support_text: RES-quinone also binds to bovine serum albumin through its cysteine residue.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Bovine serum albumin solution; also tested with plasma and hepatocytes
evidence.support_text: In the current study, apalutamide reacted with various protein sources (e.g., plasma, hepatocytes, and bovine serum albumin), while enzalutamide had little or no reaction. The binding occurred in a bovine serum albumin solution, which is a simple system, indicating that the reaction does not require metabolic activation. Reduction of binding with the inclusion of thiol nucleophiles (i.e., GSH and cysteine) was observed, suggesting that the thiols within proteins were reacting with apalutamide.

evidence.experimental_conditions: after oral or intravenous administration
evidence.support_text: D-Penicillamine was observed to bind covalently to plasma proteins including albumin, gamma globulins, and ceruloplasmin after oral or intravenous administration in humans. The protein conjugates were unstable with a half-life of 2-3 hours.

evidence.experimental_conditions: in vitro and in vivo; rat; binding to albumin; disulfide linkage
evidence.support_text: We have previously studied the metabolism of CP and found that the drug becomes extensively and covalently bound to plasma proteins both in vitro and in vivo [10]. Binding of CP is mainly to albumin, via disulphide linkage [11].

evidence.experimental_conditions: Rat liver microsomes (RLM) incubation with NADPH (complete system), [14C]clozapine, bovine serum albumin; % drug bound: 1.1%
evidence.support_text: In the complete RLM system (with NADPH), clozapine showed protein covalent binding of 106 ± 8.1 pmol/mg protein (1.1% of drug bound), significantly different from the control (P < 0.001).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Rat liver microsomes (RLM) incubation with NADPH (complete system), [14C]lamotrigine, bovine serum albumin; % drug bound: 0.17%
evidence.support_text: In the complete RLM system (with NADPH), lamotrigine showed protein covalent binding of 17.1 ± 0.86 pmol/mg protein (0.17% of drug bound), significantly different from the control (P < 0.001).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Rat liver microsomes (RLM) incubation with NADPH (incomplete system), [14C]clozapine, bovine serum albumin; % drug bound: 0.21%
evidence.support_text: In the incomplete RLM system (without NADPH), clozapine showed protein covalent binding of 20.8 ± 2.3 pmol/mg protein (0.21% of drug bound), serving as control background.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Rat liver microsomes (RLM) incubation with NADPH, [14C]lamotrigine, bovine serum albumin; 0.054% drug bound
evidence.support_text: In the RLM incubation without NADPH (incomplete system), lamotrigine showed protein covalent binding of 5.43 ± 0.70 pmol/mg protein, corresponding to 0.054% of the drug bound. The authors considered this the control background.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse bone marrow macrophages, [14C]-HQ, 1 mM H₂O₂, 37°C
evidence.support_text: Covalent labeling of protein with [14C]-HQ was observed in mouse bone marrow macrophages in the presence of H₂O₂ but not arachidonic acid.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse peritoneal macrophage lysates or purified prostaglandin-H synthase, 1 mM H₂O₂, 37°C
evidence.support_text: Hydroquinone (HQ) exhibited peroxidase-mediated binding to albumin: [14C]-HQ was observed to bind to albumin in the presence of H₂O₂ using mouse peritoneal macrophage lysates or purified prostaglandin-H synthase. Binding was inhibited by cysteine, suggesting thiol adduct formation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse epidermal JB6 cells; treatment with 8-hydroxy-α-humulene
evidence.support_text: 8-Hydroxy-α-humulene, a structural analogue of zerumbone that lacks the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl group, failed to activate Nrf2 as reported in the abstract.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mouse epidermal JB6 cells; treatment with α-humulene
evidence.support_text: α-Humulene, a structural analogue of zerumbone that lacks the α,β-unsaturated carbonyl group, failed to activate Nrf2 as reported in the abstract.

evidence.assay_type: cytokine measurement in Nrf2-knockout mouse study
evidence.experimental_conditions: Nrf2-knockout and wild-type mice; DNFB treatment; measurement of IFN-γ formation
evidence.support_text: The allergen-induced formation of the TH1 cytokine interferon-γ (IFN-γ) was completely abolished in the knockout mice, whereas the TH2 cytokine IL-4 was not affected.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Nrf2+/+ mice; bixin 200 mg/kg i.p.; 72 h post injection; skin tissue analyzed by immunoblot
evidence.support_text: Administration of bixin (200 mg/kg, i.p., 72 h after injection) upregulated cutaneous protein levels of AKR1C1 in Nrf2+/+ mice, as shown by immunoblot analysis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Nrf2+/+ mice; bixin 200 mg/kg i.p.; 72 h post injection; skin tissue analyzed by immunoblot
evidence.support_text: Administration of bixin (200 mg/kg, i.p., 72 h after injection) upregulated cutaneous protein levels of GCLM in Nrf2+/+ mice, as shown by immunoblot analysis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Nrf2+/+ mice; bixin 200 mg/kg i.p.; 72 h post injection; skin tissue analyzed by immunoblot
evidence.support_text: Administration of bixin (200 mg/kg, i.p., 72 h after injection) upregulated cutaneous protein levels of NRF2 in Nrf2+/+ mice, as shown by immunoblot analysis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Primary murine skin cells; incubated with NMP (1.0 µm and mixture particles); cells grown on glass coverslips, fixed, and stained for Nrf2 with DAPI nuclear counterstain
evidence.support_text: In primary murine skin cells, NMP exposure (1.0 µm and mixture particles) caused a strong nuclear translocation of Nrf2 as observed by immunofluorescence microscopy, indicating activation of Nrf2 signaling. The nuclear translocation was independent of NMP size.

evidence.experimental_conditions: UV-PAPC 100 µg/ml, 2 h treatment, primary human dermal fibroblasts, ImageStream analysis
evidence.support_text: Using ImageStream analysis, UV-PAPC (100 µg/ml) treatment of primary human dermal fibroblasts for 2 h resulted in strongly increased nuclear NRF2 staining, with mean peak pixel intensities rising from 179 ± 63 in untreated cells to 308 ± 94 in treated cells, as reported in Supplemental Table 5.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical application of RTA 408 to rat skin; samples taken at 4, 8, and 24 h post-dose; immunohistochemical staining for Nrf2.
evidence.support_text: Topical application of RTA 408 resulted in translocation of Nrf2 to the nucleus in skin samples. Representative slides from the 8-h post-dose subgroups are presented, and similar dose-dependent staining patterns were observed in the 4- and 24-h post-dose subgroups. Staining for Nrf2 was observed in the keratinocytes in the squamous stratified epithelial layer of the epidermis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: old rats, 40 mg/kg i.p. administration (single dose)
evidence.support_text: Administration of LA (40 mg/kg, i.p.) to old rats increased the levels of nuclear Nrf2 and GCL, and attenuated the age-related loss of GSH [67•].

evidence.experimental_conditions: Female wild-type mice; single administration of 6-HITC 15 µmol; sacrifice after 28 h; hepatic mRNA measurement
evidence.support_text: The mRNA levels of hepatic GSTP1, NQO1, and γ-GCS heavy and light chain were significantly increased by treatment with 6-HITC (15 µmol) in wild-type mice, while this induction was completely abrogated in nrf2-deficient mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: UV-PAPC 100 µg/ml and 50 µg/ml, treatment of primary human dermal fibroblasts for 3 h, nuclear extract (4 µg/well), ELISA-based quantification of NRF2 bound to consensus ARE, absorbance at 450 nm
evidence.support_text: An NRF2 activity assay using ELISA showed significant and dose-dependent activation of NRF2 binding to the antioxidant response element in dermal fibroblast nuclear extracts 3 h after treatment with UV-PAPC (100 and 50 µg/ml) compared to untreated controls (Fig. 3C).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human monocyte-derived DC (MoDC), treated with CinA, DMSO as vehicle control, assessed at 2, 4, and 6 h.
evidence.support_text: In human monocyte-derived DC (MoDC), Nrf2 was expressed after 2 h of treatment with CinA and this expression persisted at 4 h and 6 h compared to DMSO control.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human monocyte-derived DC (MoDC), treated with DNCB, DMSO as vehicle control, assessed at 2, 4, and 6 h.
evidence.support_text: In human monocyte-derived DC (MoDC), Nrf2 was expressed after 2 h of treatment with DNCB and this expression persisted at 4 h and 6 h compared to DMSO control.

evidence.experimental_conditions: topical application onto dorsal skin of hairless mice
evidence.support_text: Topical application of zerumbone onto dorsal skin of hairless mice induces activation of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) as reported in the abstract.

review_policy.eligible_subject: unique measurement-producing subject, donor, or cell-system species
